dates.notes: Adopted by the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe at the 1373rd meeting of the Ministers' Deputies on 8 April 2020. It is addressed to the governments of the 47 Council of Europe member States and has no signature, ratification or entry-into-force clause.

gaps: Non-binding: it creates no legal obligation, ratification, depositary, monitoring or enforcement.
There is no itemised list of States that have endorsed or implemented the Recommendation; it is addressed to all 47 member States.
National implementation and the Recommendation's effect in domestic law are not assessed.
The Recommendation addresses algorithmic systems broadly, not only systems that meet a particular definition of AI.
The full text is stored and segmented, but it was not read end-to-end for legal analysis in this acquisition pass.

issuer.name: Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe

languages.note: The Recommendation was adopted and published in English and French, the official languages of the Council of Europe. Only the English text was read for this record.

legal_nature.rationale: A Recommendation of the Committee of Ministers under Article 15.b of the Statute of the Council of Europe. It is a standard-setting text addressed to member States, not a treaty; it creates no legally binding obligation and has no ratification or depositary.

provenance.discovered_via: Council of Europe Committee of Ministers legal search and the official PDF; identified as a pending candidate in the AI source-family checklist.

related.note: The later binding Council of Europe framework convention on AI; the 2020 Recommendation is a precursor and a non-binding standard-setting text.
The Recommendation grounds its guidelines in the European Convention on Human Rights and the ICCPR's rights vocabulary.
A parallel non-binding intergovernmental AI recommendation adopted a year earlier.

ai_provisions: Guidelines on reviewing legislation, policies and public-sector procurement for algorithmic systems consistently with human rights.
Guidance on transparency, explainability, data protection, non-discrimination, freedom of expression and access to effective remedies.
Guidance on oversight and accountability for public and private actors across the design, development and deployment of algorithmic systems.
Recommendation that member States translate and disseminate the text and evaluate the effectiveness of measures taken.
relevance.excluded_scope: A non-binding recommendation addressed to Council of Europe member States. It creates no treaty obligation and does not establish an AI regulator or a conformity-assessment regime.
relevance.reason: Recommendation CM/Rec(2020)1 is an AI-specific human-rights instrument adopted by the Council of Europe two years before CETS 225. It had been listed as pending and was missing from the corpus, which made the Council of Europe layer look as if it began with the 2024 framework convention.

rights.note: Council of Europe terms apply. The archived official PDF is stored unaltered for research and is not relicensed.
